title: Think You Can Build a Game with AI? Think Again! - Danielle An & David Hoe, Meta
talk_summary: A Meta principal engineer and colleague demo AI-generated games (including runtime-LLM-driven NPCs) and share lessons from a year of directing AI-assisted game teams.

takeaways.technique: Pin model/prompt versions to keep agent behavior reproducible
takeaways.what_they_do: They flag that model upgrades and prompt changes silently throw off agentic systems, breaking the usual 'write code, write test, debug against a known codebase' stability model.

takeaways.technique: Treat model swaps as risky changes, not free upgrades
takeaways.what_they_do: They note that because the stack is agentic end-to-end, a model upgrade anywhere can change downstream behavior, so determinism is a cross-stack problem.

takeaways.technique: Parallel iteration instead of linear waterfall
takeaways.what_they_do: They describe moving from a linear department-by-department pipeline to parallel teams iterating in hours/days, which lets them revisit upstream decisions cheaply.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have achieved teams that are working in parallel and updates and iterations on the games are achieved in hours, days as opposed to months
